look_here_first: Find narrow cauline leaves and the long, loose blue-flowering axis. Flip to a flower CALYX: the green 15-ribbed surface (local var. grandiflora treatment) remains visible between short hairs/glands, unlike the dense white OR violet felt covering S. farinacea calyces. Check flower cluster spacing, not petal blue color alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Woody-rootstock herbaceous perennial, often upright; not a rosette. Central Texas local treatment often below 1 m.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: UT Texas var. grandiflora: only cauline leaves, narrow linear-lanceolate to linear-oblanceolate ~30–80 × 4–8 mm, mostly entire/subentire.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Long, open interrupted panicle of paired axillary cymes; lower part sometimes leafy; often only 1 flower of each cyme open at a time.

key_traits.label: Calyx
key_traits.text: Green-surfaced, bell-shaped, ~8 mm long and ca. 15-ribbed (UT local variety treatment), short-hairy with glandular hairs but not densely felted like S. farinacea.

key_traits.label: Variety caution
key_traits.text: Central Texas azure sage often var. grandiflora. New Alex Abair close photograph is Florida var. azurea; retain variety/provenance label, do not equate to local material.
